newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Turkish banks mull appeal on closed Dutch accounts.
newsitem.headline: Turkish banks mull appeal on closed Dutch accounts.

text.p: A lawyer representing four Turkish banks whose Dutch accounts were closed by ABN AMRO said on Monday he expected them to appeal against the decision of a court not to force the bank to reopen them.
"That's the intention they have, but it depends on the decision of the boards of directors of the banks in Turkey, which is expected any moment now," Guus Schipper told Reuters.
He said owned Akbank and state-owned Ziraatbank had decided to appeal against the ruling last week of the Rotterdam District Court.
Schipper said privately-owned Turkiye Is Bankasi and state-owned Emlakbank had yet to make a decision.
ABN AMRO closed the accounts of the banks, which operate in the Netherlands as representative offices without banking licences, at the request of the Dutch authorities.
The authorities believe the representative offices may have breached Dutch banking regulations by collecting deposits without holding a licence.
